# Results — Study 123 (Altman-Z) on real EDGAR + yfinance tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Altman Z-score
computed annually from EDGAR 10-K fundamentals (fiscal year *t*) and December
month-end market cap (yfinance). Forward return = calendar year *t+1*. Panel:
current S&P 500 members projected back — **survivorship-biased**; results are
upper bounds. As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Coverage | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| EDGAR (_edgar_*.parquet) | 2008–2023 | 166 tickers (all 7 concepts) | `see verify.py` |
| yfinance monthly prices | 1962–2026 | December month-end | — |
| _edgar_yrret.parquet | 1962–2026 | 420 S&P 500 tickers | — |

Z-score panel: **16 years × 166 tickers**, **1,210 valid firm-year observations**.

| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.65** |

| n years | 16 |

## Per-bucket annual means

| Bucket | Mean return/yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **Low-Z (distressed)** | +20.5% | +7.50 |
| Mid-Z (grey zone) | +21.8% | — |
| **High-Z (safe)** | +22.9% | +7.12 |
| Market EW | +21.7% | — |

*All three buckets earn ~20–23%/yr — driven by the bull market of 2008–2023,
not by Z-score differentiation. The spread is +2.4pp, far below the noise.*

| Mean return in safe zone | +20.4% |

## Survivorship-bias caveat

The EDGAR panel uses *current* S&P 500 membership projected backwards. Firms
that went bankrupt, were delisted, or exited the index between 2008 and 2023
are **absent** — which systematically inflates the low-Z (distressed) bucket
returns. In reality, many of those distressed firms would have been in the
sample and would have performed worse. The +2.4pp hedge is therefore an upper
bound; a live, unbiased implementation would likely find an even weaker or
negative spread.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Hedge HAC t = +0.65, far below the ±2 inference bar.
  Firm-level correlation = +0.013 (essentially zero). The Z-score does not
  reliably separate winners from losers within this survivorship-biased S&P 500
  universe over 2008–2023.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even the +2.36%/yr gross spread is insignificant
  and would be wiped out by transaction costs, rebalancing, and the survivorship
  adjustment. No trade.
- **Distress puzzle confirmed (weakly).** Distressed firms (low Z) do not earn
  higher returns to compensate for their risk — if anything they earn slightly
  less — consistent with the "distress puzzle" of Dichev (1998) and Campbell
  et al. (2008). But the difference is far too small and noisy to trade.
